identity.title: A CO molecular gas wind 340 pc away from the Seyfert 2 nucleus in ESO 420-G13 probes an elusive radio jet

findings_qualitative.value: Wind is redshifted, conical, starts 340 pc from the nucleus along the kinematic minor axis, with no counter-outflow

evidence.quote: The wind extends from $\sim 1.5\ensuremath{''}$ to $2.5\ensuremath{''}$ away from the nucleus ($340\, \rm{pc}$ to $600\, \rm{pc}$)

claims.hypothesis: Is there a molecular outflow in ESO 420-G13?
claims.experiment: CO(2-1) ALMA cube moment maps, channel maps, PV diagrams, 3D mask extraction
claims.result: Redshifted wind of 8.3e6 Msun at ~160 km/s, 340-600 pc from nucleus
claims.finding: A collimated molecular wind is detected

evidence.quote: A remarkable wind has been detected thanks to its redshifted CO(2–1) emission extended along the kinematic minor axis

claims.hypothesis: Is the wind jet-driven rather than driven by AGN radiation or star formation?
claims.experiment: Energy and momentum budget versus jet power, AGN radiation pressure, SNe and stellar radiation
claims.result: Mdot V = 1.4e34 exceeds stellar radiation pressure 7.7e32; AGN L/c 1.7-3.7e33 less but not excluded

evidence.quote: Therefore, neither SNe nor stellar radiation can locally drive the wind.

claims.hypothesis: Will the outflow quench star formation?
claims.experiment: Depletion time from outflow rate and total gas mass
claims.result: 23 Myr at current rate, but gas likely falls back
claims.finding: Delay rather than quenching of star formation

evidence.quote: the result of this interaction points to a delay of the star formation instead of a quenching

why_this_method.value: Robust 2.0 chosen to recover extended flux

evidence.quote: allows us to recover extended flux that might be filtered for lower robustness values

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: AGN radiation pressure, SNe and stellar radiation, minor merger and past feedback scenarios considered

evidence.quote: How do we know that the wind is not triggered by AGN radiation?
